substantive_delta: The frozen proof establishes the explicit bound 4kt(kt-1)^2 for every tagged-occurrence coverage family in the original question, independent of n,m, feature counts and feature sizes, together with a deterministic polynomial-time construction for explicitly listed incidences and item slots, including binary-encoded k,t. Disjoint Hall witnesses are restricted to cyclic categorical states; all large occurrences are exactly balanced for every state choice, while each class of small-feature interactions admits an affine coverage matrix of column l1 norm at most kt. This supplies a size-independent number of bounded-error stages.
why_nonroutine: No novelty is assigned to Hall matching, greedy classes or the known multiple-choice rounding theorem. The independent innovation is their compatible nonlinear reduction: the witness restriction preserves exact large-feature coverage without imposing an arbitrary frozen color bias on small features, and the categorical coefficient calculation still works when one feature contains multiple items of a witness. Itemwise linear rounding does not directly preserve these witnesses, and the linear grouped theorem alone does not linearize coverage. This proves a new structural bridge rather than following by substituting parameters into the inspected prior theorems. The bounded primary search found no equivalent bridge or full resolution.
significance: For this unrestricted nonlinear coverage class, every fixed t,k now has a discrepancy bound uniformly over all instance sizes; this is a qualitative resolution of the immutable polynomial-existence question, not a fixed-rank or fixed-parameter special case. The constructive method explains how to remove size dependence while retaining simultaneous control of all functions. The t,k dependence is coarse O(t^3 k^3), and no claim of matching the sharper exponents, resolving general influence-sparse Lipschitz discrepancy, worldwide priority, or STOC acceptance is made. These limitations do not erase the qualitative all-size mathematical gain.
